why: The briefs avoid both must_not items. Item 1: verifier Check 3 can't pass when slugify has no section. It lists every exported function, says "every function in that list (at least capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft) has its own section", and adds "the base README has no slugify section, so look for that one in particular." Item 2: no PASS/FAIL condition is stricter than its line. Check 1 tests exact outputs that follow from the line, and it does not require a one-character fill or check the parameter count. Check 3 defines a section only as "a heading that names it with text about it", not a required layout. The `## name(args)` style, test coverage and how the other functions behave appear only under "Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions)". The builder brief suggests a heading format, but it sets no PASS/FAIL condition, so it doesn't break the rule.
